title: Nut-Free Strawberry Shortcake Cupcakes
shortDescription: Vanilla cupcakes with a fresh strawberry compote core, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes hide a spoonful of fresh strawberry compote right in the center. The cake itself is a soft vanilla base, safe for nut-free kitchens and lunchboxes. I tested this batch three times to get the compote thick enough to stay put during baking. A cornstarch slurry is the trick that keeps it from sinking to the bottom. On top, a tall swirl of whipped vanilla frosting mimics real shortcake and whipped cream. It is light, not too sweet, and pipes beautifully. This is a great spring or summer bake for potlucks. Kids love the surprise fruit filling in the middle.
ingredients: 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tsp water
instructions: Make the compote first. Simmer diced strawberries, 3 tbsp sugar, and lemon juice in a small pot for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook 1 more minute until thick. Cool completely in the fridge.
Preheat oven to 350°F and line a muffin pan with 12 liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat butter and sugar together until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla.
Alternate adding the flour mix and milk, starting and ending with flour. Mix just until smooth.
Fill liners halfway with batter. Add 1 tsp cooled compote to the center of each, then top with more batter to cover.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes until a toothpick near the edge comes out clean.
Beat frosting butter until pale and fluffy, about 3 minutes. Add powdered sugar, cream, and vanilla, then whip 4 more minutes until light.
Pipe frosting in a tall swirl on each cupcake. Top with a small strawberry slice if you like.
tips: Chill the compote fully before filling the batter, or it will sink during baking.
Whip the frosting longer than you think you need to. A full 4 minutes makes it airy like whipped cream.
Use a piping tip with a wide opening for the tallest swirl.
Dice strawberries small, big chunks make the center heavy and can sink.

faq.question: Can I use frozen strawberries for the compote?
faq.answer: Yes, but thaw and drain them first. Extra liquid will make the compote too thin to hold its shape in the batter.

faq.question: Why did my strawberry filling sink to the bottom?
faq.answer: The compote was likely too warm or too thin. Cool it fully in the fridge and make sure the cornstarch step thickened it before filling.

faq.question: Is this frosting the same as whipped cream?
faq.answer: No, it is a whipped butter frosting that mimics the look and lightness of whipped cream but holds up better at room temperature.

faq.question: Can I make the compote ahead of time?
faq.answer: Yes, it keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days in a sealed container. Cold compote actually fills easier than warm.

conclusion: These cupcakes bring real strawberry flavor into a soft vanilla base with a fun surprise center. Bake a batch this weekend while strawberries are at their best.
